In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current state of knowledge on condensation heat transfer is still quite unsatisfactory, and that further research is needed to develop a better understanding of the physical phenomena involved and to improve the predictive capabilities of existing models.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

condensation heat transfer in the air conditioning and heat pumping industry is still a very active field, and the recent research results are expected to contribute to the improvement of the design and performance of heat exchangers.

condensation heat transfer in smooth and enhanced tubes is still a field of active research and that new correlations for the prediction of heat transfer and pressure drops during condensation are required for the design of new condensers.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of enhanced surfaces is a very powerful means to increase the performance of condensing equipment; the heat transfer enhancement factor is usually in excess of 2 and, at the same time, pressure drop is reduced with respect to plain surfaces.

the use of new working fluids, such as hydrocarbons, may lead to a significant change in the flow conditions and, consequently, to a significant change of the thermal performance of the heat exchangers, even if the same geometry is used for condensation.
the use of enhanced surfaces may lead to a significant improvement of condensation heat flux, especially when condensing mixtures are involved.
